item.title: Sunnylands in Rancho Mirage Hiring College Students as Tour Guide Interns
item.description: Sunnylands in Rancho Mirage is looking for college students interested in history, hospitality, and leadership to apply for its upcoming tour guide internship program.The paid opportunity allows students to serve as guides at the historic Annenberg Estate while also earning internship credit and gaining valuable professional development experience.According to Sunnylands officials, selected interns will participate in training during late July and August. item.title: Uber Rolls Out “Women Preferences” Feature Nationwide Allowing Riders to Request Female Drivers
item.description: In consumer news, Uber is expanding a new feature designed to give riders more choice and comfort when requesting rides.The rideshare company has rolled out its “Women Preferences” option nationwide, allowing women riders to request female drivers through the app.The feature was first introduced last August in a handful of pilot cities and later expanded to additional markets. item.title: $1 Million in Federal Funding Secured for Infrastructure Improvements at Coachella Valley Public Cemetery
item.description: The Coachella Valley Public Cemetery District has secured $1 million in federal funding to support infrastructure improvements at its cemetery grounds.The funding was obtained through a community project request by Congressman Raul Ruiz and was included in the Fiscal Year 2026 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development Appropriations Bill.The investment will help fund repairs to approximately one mile of aging roadways serving the cemetery, including those surrounding the Veterans Memorial. item.title: Is Daylight Saving Time Putting Our Health at Risk?
item.description: The annual switch to daylight saving time has once again sparked discussion about whether changing the clocks twice a year is worth the potential health impacts. Medical researchers say the sudden loss of an hour of sleep can disrupt the body’s circadian rhythm, the natural internal clock that regulates sleep, alertness, and other biological functions.Studies have found that in the days following the spring time change, there is often a noticeable increase in certain health and safety issues. item.description: The ongoing debate surrounding a local election probe has evolved beyond the details of the investigation itself, becoming an example of how public discussions increasingly unfold online. item.title: Stars Advance as Second Week of BNP Paribas Open Heats Up in Indian Wells
item.description: The second week of the BNP Paribas Open is underway at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden, with some of the sport’s biggest names competing on the stadium courts.Five-time champion Novak Djokovic battled past American Aleksandar Kovacevic in three sets to reach the fourth round of the tournament for the first time since 2017. item.title: Will Flood-Prone Drivers Have to Wait Years as Bridge Project Faces Environmental Lawsuit?
item.description: Drivers in the Coachella Valley hoping for relief from flood-prone South Palm Canyon Drive may have to wait years longer. A bridge project designed to create a floodproof route near East Bogart Trail has been delayed by at least two years following an environmental lawsuit filed by a wildlife advocacy group. item.title: Is California Penalizing New Residents with Heavy Car Taxes?
item.description: California’s strict approach to vehicle sales tax has left some new residents reeling. One recent example involves a car owner moving from Oregon, a state with no sales tax, who faced the full California sales tax on a nearly new vehicle. item.title: How Are Local Students Celebrating Literacy at Palm District High?
item.description: Palm District High School marked Read Across America Week with a unique celebration focused on child literacy. The school hosted Meet at the 50 Literacy Day, bringing kindergarten students from nearby elementary schools to its campus. Students from Carter Washington Charter and Gerald Ford Elementary participated, meeting high school seniors at the 50-yard line for reading activities.During the event, seniors read books to the children, who were also able to keep copies of the books.
